Professional Summary

I am a Ph.D. graduate in International Public Policy (Applied Economics) from the University of Tsukuba, Japan. My research focuses on international economics, international trade, development economics, spatial economics, economic geography, and applied econometrics.

My research examines how globalization, trade integration, economic shocks, and market access influence regional inequality, household welfare, and economic development, particularly in developing countries. I use quantitative methods including panel data econometrics, causal inference, spatial analysis, and satellite-based remote sensing data.
